title: Critical Signs Cheat Sheet
summary: The signs candidates mix up most, side by side, with the one detail that tells them apart.

pages.heading: Signs that look alike: orders vs warnings

blocks.text: Start with the shape: circles give orders, triangles warn and rectangles mostly inform. Then check the colour and the detail that sets each pair apart.

pairs.tell: GIVE WAY: let traffic on the major road go first, stopping only if you need to. STOP: you must stop at the line, even if the road is clear.
The triangle warns that a roundabout is ahead. The blue circle is an order: a mini-roundabout, give way to traffic from the right.
Blue circle: an order, you must turn left. Blue rectangle: information, the road is one-way.

pages.heading: Signs that look alike: entry, vehicles and speed

blocks.title: No entry, no vehicles and speed

pairs.tell: Red circle, white bar: no entry for vehicles (often the end of a one-way street). White circle, red ring: no vehicles except bicycles being pushed.
An empty red ring bans all vehicles. With a car and a motorcycle inside, it bans motor vehicles only.
A number in a red ring is the maximum speed. The white circle with a black diagonal stripe means the national limit for your vehicle and that road applies.
